channel.description: Variational circuits, quantum kernels, and the question of whether any of it beats a laptop. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Quantum machine learning preset. No pay dirt today — 3 long shots.

item.title: Linearised quantum signal processing
item.description:
Long shot Read · new method — Universal Hamiltonian Eigenvalue Transformation (UHET) can be interpreted as a (randomised) linearisation of Generalised Quantum Signal Processing (GQSP), leading to a new Universal Hamiltonian Singular Value Transformation (UHSVT).

Grade 0.908 · 1.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum Algorithm for Linear Systems of Equations” · Marek Arsenault, Hl\'er Kristj\'ansson

So what. The new Universal Hamiltonian Singular Value Transformation (UHSVT) enables efficient transformation of singular values of any arbitrary matrix encoded in a Hamiltonian, relaxing conditions required by previous QSVT-based approaches.

But. The algorithm requires the sole condition that the function f vanishes at the origin.

Tools. Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) · Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) · Universal Hamiltonian Eigenvalue Transformation (UHET) · Generalised QSP (GQSP) · Universal Hamiltonian Singular Value Transformation (UHSVT)

Abstract. Quantum functional programming has been developed through two distinct paradigms in the last few years: Quantum Signal Processing (QSP)-based methods, including the Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT), and methods based on higher-order quantum transformations, such as the Universal Hamiltonian Eigenvalue Transformation (UHET). While UHET performs functional transformations of Hamiltonian dynamics, its relationship to QSP-based techniques has remained unclear despite evident structural similarities. In this work, we resolve this gap by establishing a connection between UHET and QSP-based frameworks; specifically, we show that UHET can be interpreted as a (randomised) linearisation of Generalised QSP (GQSP). Building on this result, we introduce a linearised variant of (Hamiltonian-based) QSVT, which we call Universal Hamiltonian Singular Value Transformation (UHSVT), that enables the efficient transformation of the singular values of any arbitrary matrix $A$ encoded in a block of a Hamiltonian, whose dynamics is accessible as a black box, by any sufficiently differentiable complex-valued function $f$. Our algorithm requires the sole condition that $f$ vanishes at the origin, in contrast to previous QSVT-based approaches that assumed either a lower bound on the singular values of $A$ or the ability to perform $X$-rotation gates on the induced two-dimensional 'qubitised' subspace.

item.title: Resource-efficient quantum eigenvalue transform with commutator scaling
item.description:
Long shot Read · new method — New quantum algorithms for eigenvalue transforms achieve commutator scaling, lower circuit depth, and require only a single ancillary qubit.

Grade 0.907 · 1.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum Algorithm for Linear Systems of Equations” · Arul Rhik Mazumder, James D. Watson, Samson Wang

So what. This method offers more resource-efficient quantum algorithms for applications like phase estimation, Green's function evaluation, and measurement distribution estimation.

But. The method's significantly shallower circuit depths are confirmed in certain parameter regimes and its application is heuristic.

Tools. quantum algorithms · product formulae circuits · classical postprocessing · Richardson extrapolation

Abstract. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating properties of general matrix functions of Hermitian matrices, with applications to phase estimation, Green's function evaluation, and estimating measurement distributions of time-evolved states. The resulting methods exhibit commutator scaling in matrix parameters similar to that usually found for product formulae, lower circuit depth in other parameters, and require only a single ancillary qubit. Our central primitive consists of classically postprocessing randomly chosen product formulae circuits, which mathematically corresponds to an approximation of a Richardson extrapolation. Within our framework, we introduce a protocol for approximating the measurement distributions of quantum states, extending beyond standard observable estimation. We also provide tightened gate complexity bounds for practically relevant systems, including those with k-local interactions, long-tailed matrix ensembles, and conserved quantities. Finally, numerical experiments confirm that our method can achieve significantly shallower circuit depths than standard product formulae in certain parameter regimes, and highlight the potential of their heuristic application.

item.title: Classical Limits of Spectral Filtering in Quantum Generative Models
item.description:
Long shot Read · new result — Magnitude (attenuating) filters in quantum generative models do not create a quantum-classical separation.

Grade 0.906 · 1.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Effect of data encoding on the expressive power of variational quantum-machine-…” · Marco Roth

So what. Researchers using spectral filtering for regularization in quantum generative models should note that magnitude filters do not provide a quantum-classical separation, with any such separation inherited from the spectral phase of the input state.

But. The dichotomy for magnitude filters holds at a fixed affordability threshold.

Tools. spectral filtering · quantum generative models · quantum Fourier transform · circuit Born machines · numerical experiments

Abstract. Spectral filtering has been proposed as a route to regularization in quantum generative models: the quantum Fourier transform exposes the amplitude spectrum of a quantum circuit Born machine, and a diagonal filter suppresses the high frequencies associated with finite-sample noise, an operation whose classical counterpart seemingly requires manipulating an exponentially long amplitude vector. We examine whether this coherent operation produces anything that classical post-processing of samples from the unfiltered model cannot match. Measuring the filter against convolution with a symmetric probability kernel at matched sampling cost, which accounts for the post-selection overhead of attenuation, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the gap between the two to vanish. Magnitude (attenuating) filters obey a dichotomy: at a fixed affordability threshold, the filtered output is either a constant-size Fourier object with an efficient classical sampler, or the passband must widen until no fixed frequency is attenuated and the filter no longer smooths. In neither case does the filter create a quantum-classical separation. Whatever separation survives is inherited from the spectral phase of the input state. Numerical experiments on trained circuit Born machines confirm the classification and show that the deciding phases are invisible to the Born-rule training loss and set by the initialization. Within the diagonal family, pure phase filters remain the only spectral operations exempt from these constraints.
